steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A good essay has a clear structure: introduction, 3-4 developed paragraphs, and a conclusion

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The introduction should define key terms, show understanding of the question, and indicate your line of argument

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Use the PEEL structure for paragraphs: Point, Evidence, Explanation, Link back to the question

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Each paragraph should focus on one main point that directly answers the question

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What does PEEL stand for and why is it useful? | Q: What should an introduction include? | Q: Why is a conclusion essential in an OCR J198 essay?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Point, Evidence, Explanation, Link. It ensures each paragraph has a clear focus, is supported by specific evidence, is developed through explanation, and connects back to the question. | Definition of key terms, understanding of the question, and an indication of your line of argument. | Because the conclusion is where you deliver your direct, justified judgement — without it, you cannot access the top mark band.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Spend 2-3 minutes planning your essay structure before writing — it saves time overall Start each paragraph with a clear topic sentence that directly relates to the question Use specific named evidence: 'In 490 BCE at Marathon...' rather than 'the Greeks won a battle' In your conclusion, don't just repeat what you said — make a clear, definitive judgement If you're running out of time, write a brief conclusion — it's better than none at all
